items.title: Tor against the quotients by powers of an ideal is eventually strictly pro-zero
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that for a finite module over a Noetherian ring and a fixed positive degree, the Tor groups against the successive quotients by powers of an ideal form a strictly pro-zero system. The statement carries a literature reference with a comment on its wording, and the text supplies its own proof: for degree one the Tor group is identified with a quotient of an intersection of the kernel with a power of the ideal in a free module, and Artin-Rees bounds that intersection inside a suitable smaller power of the kernel, which is exactly the required vanishing on a tail; higher degrees are reduced to degree one by the usual dimension shift along the short exact sequence.
